text:
rachel: Prod linkcheck: /howto/integrate#sdk-quickstart fails (404). The heading is present but the anchor in the HTML is different. Page was migrated from mkdocs and has frontmatter `title: SDK Quickstart` plus an H2 `## SDK quickstart` — could that duplicate/normalize differently?

kevin: Yeah, frontmatter titles sometimes produce a different slug than the in-page heading. Docusaurus prefers the first heading, but our legacy migration emitted frontmatter-based anchors for redirects. That mismatch can create two different anchors (`sdk-quickstart` vs `sdk-quickstart-1`).

philip: Repro: inspect built HTML id attrs:

```bash
# build site locally and grep the file for id attributes
yarn docs:build && grep -n "id=\".*sdk-quickstart" build/*/howto/integrate.html || true
```

I saw `id="sdk-quickstart-1"` in the output. Legacy slugify gave `sdk-quickstart`. Linkcheck was looking for the latter.

rachel: Is the duplication from title + heading or duplicate headings during migrate?

kevin: Migration left a hidden heading token in some pages (we had `<!-- mkdocs:title -->` markers for back-compat). Those markers can become empty headers that bump subsequent IDs. If the first ID is taken it adds a suffix `-1` which breaks existing anchors.

philip: Quick fixes:
1) Run a hygiene script to remove `<!-- mkdocs:title -->` markers and any phantom headings in migrated files.
2) In the migration pipeline, canonicalize on either frontmatter or first heading and remove the other.
3) Emit redirect entries for known changed anchors using our inbound-links list.

rachel: I'll open a small PR that: strips phantom markers, regenerates slugs, and runs linkcheck across a sampled set of migrated pages. Will include a smoke test that builds HTML and asserts no `-1` suffix for anchors that appear in the inbound list.

kevin: Also add a lint rule in docs-ci that runs a fast ID collision check on modified MDX files — fail the PR if a heading produces an ID that ends in `-1` unless explicitly allowed.

philip: Good idea. For redirects, we should only add mappings for anchors that show inbound traffic (we have the analytics export). I'll wire that filter into the redirect generator.

docs-bot: New PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5677 by rachel 1 remove mkdocs markers, add anchor hygiene + CI lint

ci-bot: docs-ci (linkcheck) queued. Rerun after PR merge.
